ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening at onboarding, before incorporation registration, and on an ongoing basis against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the U.S. OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, INTERPOL notices, and Panama’s UAF and national designated-persons databases. All ultimate beneficial owners, directors, officers, shareholders, and counter-parties must be screened. PEPs and their family members and close associates require enhanced due diligence, including source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification, senior-management approval, and enhanced monitoring for ACH and bank-wire payment rails.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá — Portal de Servicios en Línea, Consulta y Reserva de Denominaciones para Personas Jurídicas
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official working language of the Public Registry is Spanish. A corporation may adopt a name in any language provided it is written in Latin or Roman script; non-Spanish names must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet. The corporate denomination must clearly include the Spanish legal-entity form, either ‘Sociedad Anónima’ or the abbreviation ‘S.A.’. Names in a foreign script or language must not obscure the Panamanian corporate form, and the Public Registry may require a Spanish translation or transliteration of the proposed denominación for distinctiveness and publication purposes.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected by the Registro Público, counsel must file a written Recurso de Reconsideración before the same Registry unit within five (5) business days of notification, attaching the rejection decision and legal argument that the name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered denomination and does not violate public-order restrictions. If reconsideration is denied, the applicant may file an appeal to the Director General del Registro Público within ten (10) business days. Ultimately, an adverse decision may be challenged through a Demanda Contencioso-Administrativa before the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso Administrativo de la Corte Suprema de Justicia. A new name-reservation application may be filed at any time upon payment of the applicable statutory fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: The statutory registered office may be satisfied by the resident agent’s physical office address. However, for a customs-bonded road feeder truck fleet, a pure virtual office is not permissible for the operational licence: the company must demonstrate physical commercial substance in Panama, including a leased or owned facility for fleet parking, GPS and seal monitoring, maintenance records, and the registered tax/authorized customs domicile before the Dirección General de Aduanas and the Panamanian transport authority will issue the corresponding customs bonded carrier and vehicle operating permits.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High — estimated at greater than 80% within the first 12 months of obtaining an active customs bonded carrier licence. Unannounced on-site inspections are common at fleet yards and bonded parking facilities; Aduanas and transport regulators will also conduct periodic cargo seal, GPS, odometer, and manifest audits at the registered operational garage and at airport feeder facilities.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Código de Comercio de la República de Panamá, Book II, Title I (Sociedades Anónimas), as complemented and amended by Ley No. 32 de 1927 (Ley sobre Sociedades Anónimas) and subsequent reforms; inscription regime governed by the Ley del Registro Público and its implementing regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Mercantile Section), Dirección Nacional del Registro Público, Ministerio de Gobierno
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (Public Deed of Incorporation) executed before a Notario Público and inscribed in the Registro Público, resulting in the Folio Electrónico and Certificado de Registro de la Sociedad
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required under Panamanian law; the deed must state an authorized capital (commonly US$10,000 divided into common shares). Capital contributions may remain unpaid until called, and no escrow or bank deposit obligation is imposed at incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD MEETING OF [COMPANY NAME], S.A., PANAMA CITY, REPUBLIC OF PANAMA — [Date]. Present: all named directors; notice duly waived. (1) CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: the Board accepts subscription for 10,000 common shares of US$1.00 par value each, records issuance in the Shareholders' Register, and confirms receipt of the agreed contributions. (2) REGISTERED OFFICE: the corporate domicile is fixed at [Registered Address], Panama City, Panama, and the Resident Agent is expressly ratified. (3) OFFICERS: the Board appoints [Name] as President, [Name] as Secretary, and [Name] as Treasurer, each to hold office until successors are duly elected. (4) BANKING AND COUNTERSIGNATURE: the President and Treasurer are jointly authorized to open bank accounts, endorse instruments, and execute operational documents. Unanimously adopted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and Availability Certification (Pesquisadora de Nombre)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Name Search Desk) or a Notario Público acting through an authorized corporate agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a written application listing up to three proposed corporate names in the format [Name], S.A. The registry performs a titular search and issues a name availability certificate. The certificate must be secured before execution of the public deed and used within its validity period; obtain the certified name in the exact form to be inscribed.
required_dossiers: Name search application signed by the incorporator or its attorney-in-fact
Certified copy of the incorporator's passport or national ID
Payment receipt for the name search and certification fee
Notarized power of attorney if acting through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused or conflicts with an existing registration, promptly re-submit the remaining alternative names and pay the corresponding certification fee; no substantive penalty or waiting period is imposed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Public Deed of Incorporation (Escritura Pública de Constitución)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notario Público of the Republic of Panama (Notaría of the Circuit of Panama)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary drafts the escritura pública de constitución containing the corporate name, registered office, corporate purpose (including bonded cargo trucking and logistics services), authorized capital, share classes, initial directors, and resident agent appointment. All incorporators or their legal representatives must appear in person before the notary to execute the deed. The duly executed first-copy protocol is then prepared for registry presentation.
required_dossiers: Certified name availability certificate from Step 1
Passport copies and proof of address of all shareholders and directors
Notarized power of attorney where incorporators are represented
Draft bylaws (estatutos) including board powers and quorum rules
Consent letter and identification of the Resident Agent (Agente Residente)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Notarial inconsistencies are cured by amending the draft before signature; post-execution errors are remedied through a separate escritura de aclaración y corrección executed by the board and the resident agent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Fiscal Duties and Registry Inscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Sede del Registro Público (Mercantile Registration Window) and Banco Nacional de Panamá or other authorized fiscal collection offices
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pay the incorporation tax (impuesto de incorporación), timbre fiscal, and registry inscription fees at the authorized bank or collection point. Submit the certified first copy of the public deed together with the payment vouchers, name certificate, and filing form to the Mercantile Section of the Public Registry. The registry verifies the deed, assigns the corporate folio number, and records the company as legally existing.
required_dossiers: Certified first copy of the Escritura Pública de Constitución
Original payment receipts for incorporation tax and registry fees
Name availability certificate
Registry inscription application form (boleta de inscripción)
Power of attorney if the filing is made by a registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a nota de reparo or defect note, the identified deficiencies must be cured and the document re-presented within the statutory period (normally 15 working days). Unresolved objections may be appealed administratively or corrected through a clarifying deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Corporate Folio Certificate and Legalization of Corporate Books
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Certification Desk and Online Services)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After inscription, request a certified certificate (antecedentes) from the corporate folio confirming the company name, incorporation date, registered office, capital, directors, and resident agent. This certificate constitutes conclusive evidence of legal existence for banks, tax authorities, and regulators. Simultaneously, present the corporate books (shareholders' register, minutes books of shareholders and directors) for legalization before the Public Registry, enabling valid recordation of future resolutions.
required_dossiers: Corporate folio number assigned upon inscription
Application for certified certificate of legal existence
Payment receipt for certification fee
Corporate books: Libro de Registro de Acciones, Libro de Actas de Junta Directiva, Libro de Actas de Accionistas
Identification of the legal representative or registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Discrepancies in the folio are corrected by filing a written correction request supported by the public deed; clerical omissions are cured by presenting the clarifying deed to the same registry section.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registry, Municipal Operating Permit, and Resident Agent Domicile Validation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Municipio de Panamá (Tesorería Municipal); Contraloría General de la República (for ROF invoicing reference)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) application before DGI and obtain the company's RUC number; register the corporate tax obligations (ISR, ITBMS) and obtain the ROF invoicing reference where commercial invoicing is required. At the municipal level, apply for the Aviso de Operación and municipal patent identifying the bonded trucking activity and the registered address; update the resident agent's domicile records with supporting address documentation. The RUC and municipal permits are prerequisites for operational licensing in Stage 2.
required_dossiers: Certified corporate folio certificate (antecedentes), issued in Step 4
Board resolution appointing officers and approving the registered office
Passport or ID copies of the legal representatives and directors
Domicile verification document: lease agreement or title deed of registered address
Duly completed DGI RUC application forms
Municipal Aviso de Operación application and patent fee schedule
ROF/Contraloría registration evidence where applicable for invoicing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI or the municipality returns a defect note, correct the filed forms and re-submit within the stated curing period; where the activity description or domicile is inaccurate, file an amendment before the Public Registry and update the municipal record accordingly.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Autoridad de Tránsito y Transporte Terrestre (ATTT) jointly with the Dirección General de Aduanas (DGA), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; airside access additionally coordinated with the airport concessionaire (Tocumen, S.A.) and Autoridad de Aeronáutica Civil (AAC)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Operación de Transporte de Carga por Carretera (ATTT) and Autorización de Transportista Aduanero under the Régimen de Tránsito y Precinto (DGA) — Bonded Truck Fleet Operation License for Customs-Sealed Airport Feeder Services

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE), Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II (moderate impact) requiring an Estudio de Impacto Ambiental Preliminar (EsIA Preliminar / Diagnóstico Ambiental) for fleet yards, truck-washing, and maintenance facilities; Category I (registration/aviso) may apply for pure parking and storage operations, subject to MiAMBIENTE screening and classification criteria.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wash-bay wastewater must be pre-treated through oil-water separators and comply with Panamanian effluent technical norms (DGNTI-COPANIT) and municipal sewer discharge limits; hazardous wastes (used oils, filters, batteries) must be handled and disposed of by licensed waste operators; heavy-duty diesel vehicles must pass mandatory periodic Revisión Técnica Vehicular emissions and opacity testing under the ATTT inspection scheme; any VOC-emitting operations (e.g., spray painting) require suppression equipment to protect ambient air quality.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá covering the fleet yard, administrative offices, and fuel or maintenance areas; structural/load inspection and occupancy permit from the Municipio de Panamá; occupational health and safety clearance from the Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) including workplace risk prevention programs, PPE provision, and the designation of a safety officer; airport-side personnel security clearance and driver credential verification required for air cargo ramp access.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direccion General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economia y Finanzas (MEF), Republic of Panama; taxpayer portal: https://dgi.mef.gob.pa; electronic filing and e-invoicing platform: SITeD and the DGI Facturacion Electronica portal. Customs administration is separate, under the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA), operating the SICE single window for export and bonded transit declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the Sociedad Anonima (S.A.) at the Registro Publico de Panama through a licensed resident agent (abogado idoneo) and obtain the Public Registry certificate (testimonio) with the registered corporate bylaws and appointment of officers. Step 2: File the municipal Aviso de Operacion (business notice) with the Alcaldia of the operational domicile and obtain the municipal operating license/patente. Step 3: Procure from the government electronic signature authority (AIG) a certified digital signature (Firma Digital) for the legal representative, required for all DGI filings. Step 4: Submit the RUC (Registro Unico de Contribuyente) application at DGI presenting the Public Registry attestation, Aviso de Operacion, proof of fiscal domicile, notarized and apostilled powers of attorney, and identification of the legal representative; the RUC certificate is generally issued within 5-10 business days. Step 5: Register the ITBMS general-regime status, enroll in the DGI electronic invoicing program, and register the employer payroll planilla with the DGI. Step 6 (foreign entities without a Panamanian incorporation): a non-resident entity must appoint a resident fiscal agent, register a branch or permanent establishment at the Registro Publico, and obtain a local RUC through the same DGI procedure; the RUC is the exclusive statutory tax identity for issuing invoices and filing returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Territorial_Scope: the S.A. is a Panamanian resident taxpayer taxed at entity level on Panama-source income only; corporate income tax (ISR) applies at 15% on the first B/. 50,000 of net taxable income and 25% on the excess; foreign-source income and capital gains realized abroad are outside the Panamanian tax net; dividends paid from Panama-source profits are subject to a 10% withholding tax (5% for shares listed on the Bolsa de Valores de Panama); there are no CFC rules, no worldwide consolidation, and no general thin-capitalization limitation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not operate a US-style check-the-box election or a BEPS Action 2 hybrid mismatch election, and hybrid mismatch rules have not been enacted. Available statutory elections: (1) the small-taxpayer simplified regime (REPEC) - an S.A. with annual gross revenue not exceeding B/. 36,000 may elect a monthly presumptive quota in lieu of regular ISR and ITBMS filing obligations; (2) the reduced 5% dividend withholding rate election for S.A. issuers with shares admitted to trading on the Bolsa de Valores de Panama; (3) the free-zone or bonded-operator election allowing suspension of ITBMS on qualifying intra-zone and re-export movements where the operator holds an ANA or Ministerio de Comercio license; and (4) the accelerated depreciation election for commercial vehicle and GPS fleet assets under DGI guidelines, requiring a written accounting policy filed with the annual ISR return.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) - Panama's VAT-type indirect tax under Decreto de Gabinete No. 22 de 1976 and subsequent amendments contained in the Codigo Fiscal (Titulo II, Libro VII).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: General regime: no de minimis threshold - any person habitually transferring movable goods or providing services in Panama, including a non-resident acting through a Panamanian permanent establishment, must register for ITBMS from the first taxable operation. Simplified REPEC small-taxpayer threshold: cumulative annual gross revenue up to B/. 36,000 (Balboas 36,000, equal to USD 36,000 under the fixed 1:1 peg) permits election of the monthly presumptive quota regime replacing regular ITBMS/ISR declarations. The bonded truck fleet operator providing international airport feeder services is in the general regime and must file monthly ITBMS returns.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic invoicing (Facturacion Electronica) is mandatory for general-regime taxpayers, phased in since 2021 and currently required for all RUC holders issuing commercial documents. Permitted issuance channels: (a) the DGI web portal (eFactura) using the holder's certified digital signature, (b) DGI-approved fiscal POS equipment or fiscal printers, and (c) machine-to-machine API (M2M/ERP) integration directly from the carrier's transport management system. Each invoice in XML/CII format must be transmitted to DGI for real-time automated validation before the fiscal copy is delivered; the DGI returns an acceptance token (respuesta de validacion) and a sequential fiscal authorization number that must be reproduced on the customer copy, including a machine-readable QR element. Taxpayers must batch-report daily sales, preserve the DGI-validated XML for at least 7 years, and reconcile e-invoice data with monthly ITBMS returns. Export declarations are separately cleared through the ANA SICE single window, which interfaces with the DGI for export VAT substantiation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% ITBMS) applies to (i) the definitive export of movable goods evidenced by a qualifying ANA customs export declaration and (ii) services rendered in Panama for the direct use or benefit of a non-resident person where the economic benefit occurs abroad, including international transport and ancillary services. For the GPS-sealed bonded road-feeder fleet serving Tocumen International Airport (PTY), the feeder service qualifies for 0% ITBMS where all of the following conditions are met: (a) the transport contract is concluded with a non-resident airline, consolidator, or global freight forwarder; (b) the truck movement is covered by a master or house air waybill (MAWB/HAWB) or a multimodal transport document naming the non-resident principal; (c) the cargo is consigned for immediate exportation and remains under customs bonded control from pickup to aircraft loading; and (d) invoicing is in US dollars to the offshore counterparty. Input ITBMS attributable to zero-rated export feeder services is creditable against taxable output ITBMS and the excess is refundable or carried forward under DGI rules. Domestic-only pick-up and delivery legs not covered by an international waybill remain subject to 7% ITBMS.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The bonded truck fleet operator may claim 0% ITBMS on qualifying export feeder services when the cargo is in customs bonded transit to an international flight and the commercial risk and contracting party are non-resident. The exporter of record must hold the RUC and issue the invoice with the DGI-validated electronic fiscal code indicating ITBMS 0%. The claim must be substantiated with customs and commercial documentation showing the physical exit of goods from the national customs territory within a reasonable time after invoicing.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaracion de Exportacion) filed through the ANA SICE single window, bearing the electronic acknowledgment and export stamp of the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas.
Customs Transit Declaration and carrier road manifest (Hoja de Ruta / Manifiesto de Carga Terrestre) evidencing the regulated bonded movement of the sealed unit from origin to the departure airport.
Master or house Air Waybill (MAWB/HAWB) or multimodal transport waybill issued to the non-resident principal, evidencing the international carriage of the consignment.
Commercial invoice issued at 0% ITBMS with the DGI-validated fiscal number, describing the ISIC 5222 road-feeder service and referencing the related AWB and customs declaration.
GPS seal tracking report and delivery receipt (carta de porte) demonstrating uninterrupted bonded custody from collection to aircraft-side delivery.
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT MT103, or bank credit advice showing receipt of USD funds from the non-resident counterparty within the 180-day benchmark.
Packing list and consignment security/SSL certificate, plus, upon DGI audit request, the DGI export certification form and the carrier's ANA bonded operator license.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI may audit ITBMS positions within a 5-year limitation period. Where 0% export treatment is applied without valid SICE export declarations, matched air waybills, and foreign remittance evidence, DGI will reverse the zero-rating, assess the unpaid 7% ITBMS, charge moratory interest, and impose administrative fines ranging from 25% to 100% of the omitted tax, or up to 200% for repeated or fraudulent conduct. Refunds already claimed are clawed back with interest and penalty. False attestation of exportation (including fabricated waybills, sham transit declarations, or simulated off-shore contracts) constitutes tax fraud and may trigger criminal prosecution with fines and imprisonment under the Codigo Penal, alongside administrative disqualification. ANA may additionally suspend or revoke the bonded truck fleet operator's customs license and its Operador Economico Autorizado (AEO) status, barring the entity from the bonded transit regime.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No Panamanian central bank exists; the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) acts as the prudential banking supervisor. The U.S. dollar is legal tender under Law 84 of 1946 and Decree Law 14 of 1973.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates a fully dollarized monetary system with no local paper currency. Current and capital account items are freely convertible; there are no exchange controls, no capital gains repatriation restrictions, and no obligatory surrender of export proceeds. Profit remittance is subject only to ordinary corporate income tax if sourced to Panama income and withholding tax for distributions to non-resident shareholders at applicable treaty or statutory rate.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion ratio exists under Panamanian law. Export receipts may be retained in any currency, although business must be conducted in U.S. dollars for local clearing and SBP-regulated bank settlement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (USD current account) with optional payroll and treasury sweep
Capital Escrow Account for corporate bond-style collateral and regulated Customs Bonded Trucking guarantees
Operational Account with dedicated SWIFT and ACH settlement facilities for cross-border road feeder services

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium: Panama does not currently issue EU-style e-money institution (EMI) licenses, but SBP-regulated 'fintech' service corporations may operate under the Panama Financial Innovation Law (Law 42 of 2023) and obtain a 'Servicios Financieros' license for payments and digital wallets. Non-regulated offshore EMIs cannot clear Panamanian ACH or U.S. dollar point-of-sale transactions without a sponsoring local bank and are viewed as unlicensed financial institutions by SBP for AML/CFT purposes.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person attendance by the entity's ultimate beneficial owners and at least one authorized director is expected under SBP's customer due diligence rules (Acuerdo 01-2020 and SBP Circulars). Remote opening is permitted only for existing bank customers, and for new customers requires notarized corporate resolutions, apostilled powers of attorney, video identification by a compliance officer, and enhanced due diligence when the entity operates in a customs-trade intermediary sector.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bonded trucking entity newly incorporated with no audited local financial history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited parent company financials, certified tax filings, customs bonded warehouse license, GPS fleet registration certificates, bank reference from a recognized foreign bank, and a sworn statement of source of funds for every initial deposit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership spread across bearer-share jurisdictions and registered agents
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete notarized ownership chain, nominee declarations, apostilled UBO register (if available), legal opinion from Panamanian counsel confirming that shares have been immobilized with the Secretariat of the Mercantile Registry, and identity documents for all natural person owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cargo or third-party disbursement activity with mixed payees
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial contracts with airlines, ground handlers, and customs brokers; prior monthly client lists; invoice rationalization memo; route shipment logs tied to custom entry numbers; and an AML officer-in-charge statement attesting to real economic purpose.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital is wired in U.S. dollars via CHIPS or Fedwire to the corporate operating account using SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'TF' (transfer) or 'Equity Contribution' plus a free-format description naming the project and customs license number. The capital injection must be backed by a board resolution, updated corporate register, a source-of-wealth letter signed by the shareholder, and a notarized UBO attestation to pass SBP onboarding and transaction monitoring.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements use SWIFT MT103 for direct foreign supplier wires and documentary collections; for higher-value airport fuel, airport landing charges, and customs duty payments, commercial letters of credit are issued via SWIFT MT700. Domestic concessionaire, truck-toll, port authority, and customs terminal charges are settled using Panama's ACH direct debit network with intraday USD clearing under the Panama ACH (CMI) system operated by Centro de Procesamiento y Compensación (CPC).
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot USD/EUR, USD/CNH, and USD/CHF trades through SBP-licensed banks
Outright USD/EUR and USD/CNH forward contracts (10 business days to 12 months) with no underlying interbank exchange-control restriction
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on convertible emerging-market currencies for counterparty payments linked to route feeder operations, provided the NDF contract settles in USD
Cross-currency swaps for long-term capital leases of truck fleets financed from Europe and Asia, net-settled in USD

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax (Annuidad) for Panama Sociedad Anónima
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 15 January of each calendar year; newly incorporated corporations pay prorated first annuity at registration, with subsequent annuities due each 15 January.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory interest plus late-payment penalty; outstanding annuity for three consecutive years permits administrative strike-off by the Public Registry, with loss of corporate legal capacity and inability to operate customs-bonded trucking authorizations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal Operation Notice Renewal (Aviso de Operación) for Airport Feeder Trucking Activities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipio de Panamá - Dirección de Rentas Municipales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between 1 January and 31 March for the calendar year in which operations occur.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Suspension of municipal operating authorization, monthly municipal surcharge, and inability to process customs-bonded cargo entries at terminal facilities due to absence of a current Aviso de Operación.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Owner Sworn Annual Confirmation (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) - Registro de Beneficiario Final
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 30 April following the 31 December fiscal year-end, and within 30 days after any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership percentages.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly monetary fines up to USD 500 per month; refusal by the Public Registry to record subsequent share transfers or corporate changes; personal liability of directors and residents agents for non-presentation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada de ISR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) - Treasury Taxpayer Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal year 1 January to 31 December; return due on or before 31 March of the following year, accompanied by payment of any remaining applicable territorial tax balance.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-payment surcharge, interest accrual, and a 3% per-month fine until filing; issuance of tax clearance certificates is blocked, which stops customs carrier license renewal and Movement Control File processing for bonded trucking.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Renewal of Customs Bonded Carrier Licence and Surety Bond (Operación de Transporte de Alta Vigilancia Aduanera)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas de Panamá (ANA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually 30 days before the licence anniversary date; the surety bond must be renewed concurrently with ANA's annual fleet inspection and GPS seal verification.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Suspension of bonded transport authorization, freezing of the customs bond, and potential seizure of trailer units for unauthorized operation without a valid renewal certificate.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Panama S.A. is subject to compulsory independent audit when annual gross taxable revenues exceed USD 1,000,000, total assets exceed USD 3,000,000, or when the DGI formally requires audited financial statements under the Panamanian Fiscal Code; customs-bonded operators must additionally present a historical compliance audit of bonded vehicular movements and cargo manifests to the ANA for annual authorization renewal.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards as adopted in Panama ('NIIF/IFRS'), governed by Law 57 of 2002 and DGI Resolution No. 700-0031; qualifying small and medium entities may apply the IFRS for SMEs standard while maintaining general-ledger consistency.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each Sociedad Anónima must keep a validated Register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners and submit an annual sworn confirmation to DGI declaring every individual with direct or indirect ownership of at least 10%, voting rights of at least 15%, or control by any other means. The confirmation is due annually by 30 April; any share transfer that changes proportionate ownership must be updated in the DGI beneficiary-owner platform within 30 days, with the updated printout maintained at the statutory registered office before the transfer is recognized by the Public Registry.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (Libro de Actas y Resoluciones)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (top marginal rate; progressive scale applied to net taxable income before the 10% dividend tax: 0% on the first USD 50,000; 15% on the band from USD 50,001 to USD 1,500,000; 25% above USD 1,500,000)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation exempts foreign-source income. The Customs Bonded Truck Fleet operator benefits from: (i) exemption from ISR on revenues from international transit segments performed outside Panamanian territory if supported by GPS logs and customs manifests; (ii) accelerated depreciation for heavy transport vehicles; (iii) zero WHT on interest paid to non-resident banks without a Panama permanent establishment; (iv) the CAIR (Cálculo del Ajuste por Inflación) minimum tax of 1% of net assets acts as an alternative minimum tax, not a preferential regime. No tax holidays apply to this ISIC 5222 activity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual return: Form 744 (Declaración Jurada de Impuesto sobre la Renta); quarterly prepayment returns: Form 745; transfer pricing annual informativity: Form 750. Electronic filing is mandatory through the DGI eTax portal (SITIO – Sistema de Información Tributaria en Línea), accessible at https://etax.dgi.gob.pa; the taxpayer must hold a valid RUC and an accepted digital certificate or e-signature profile.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (Form 744) plus quarterly advance returns (Form 745) due on 15 April, 15 July, 15 October, and 15 January of the following year, computed on the prior year's ISR liability; the final annual return reconciles the quarterly prepayments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Form 744 must be filed within three (3) months after the close of the fiscal year (Article 713-A, Código Fiscal). For a calendar-year taxpayer, the deadline is 31 March. No automatic extension is granted; the DGI may impose surcharges from the day after the deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part A, Box 1 – RUC / Folio / Fiscal Year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification number (Registro Único de Contribuyente), entity folio in the Public Registry, and the tax period (e.g., 1 January – 31 December).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Panama S.A. held by non-residents, this box must identify the legal representative in Panama and the permanent agent designated before the DGI; absence of a Panamanian resident agent is a filing obstacle.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 – Ingresos Brutos de Fuente Panameña (Gross Panamanian-source revenue)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All gross revenue derived from bonded road feeder transport, customs storage cross-docking, and related logistics services physically performed within Panama, including the domestic leg of international airport cargo.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all fees invoiced to airlines, freight forwarders, and customs brokers for services rendered inside Panama. GPS-tracked kilometres outside Panamanian territory with corresponding customs seals may be allocated to foreign-source income and excluded, but the allocation must be supported by trip manifests.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 – Ingresos de Fuente Extranjera (Foreign-source revenue)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue from international transit segments legally sourced outside Panama (territoriality principle), reported on a separate line and memorandum schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must note that foreign-source income is exempt from Panamanian ISR, but related expenses are not deductible against Panamanian-source income and must be traced separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 – Costos y Gastos Deducibles (Deductible costs and expenses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fuel, tolls, GPS telematics subscriptions, customs bonds, insurance, salaries, depreciation of trucks/trailers, airport handling fees, maintenance, and licenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions require possession of legally issued receipts (Facturas), tax identification of the supplier, and bank wire/ACH evidence. Intercompany invoices from a non-resident related party are deductible only if the transaction is arm's length and the TP disclosure is attached.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 – Ajuste por Inflación Calculado (CAIR) – 1% net-asset minimum tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the alternative minimum tax: 1% of net assets (patrimonio) at fiscal year-end, compared against the ordinary ISR; the higher amount is paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A low-substance holding structure without trucks, employees, or premises in Panama nonetheless triggers the CAIR on gross assets; non-residents should verify that lease assets are not falsely booked to inflate net worth.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 – Créditos Fiscales por Anticipos y Retenciones (Prepayments and WHT credits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Form 745 quarterly prepayments, 2% or 5% DGI withholding credits deducted by clients on invoice payments, and any foreign tax credits only if a treaty applies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities with no Panamanian permanent establishment are not entitled to offset credits against the 10% dividend tax; the Form 744 credit box is reserved for the local operating entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 – Operaciones con Partes Relacionadas (Related-party disclosure / Form 750 annex)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory disclosure of intercompany transactions (transport fees, management charges, intercompany debt interest) with related parties, including foreign airport logistics hubs and parent entities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If aggregate related-party transactions exceed USD 250,000 in the fiscal year, attach the Local File and Form 750; non-resident shareholder loans above 3:1 debt-to-equity ratios are scrutinized under the thin-capitalization practice.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 – Utilidad Neta y Cálculo del ISR Causado (Taxable income and ISR computation)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after the 5-year loss carryforward, application of the progressive scale (0% / 15% / 25%), and deduction of prepayments to arrive at the balance payable or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents are not subject to a branch return, but the Panama entity must declare and pay; the resulting after-tax profit becomes the base for the 10% dividend WHT when repatriated.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: fine up to USD 10,000 per return, or up to 5% of gross income for large taxpayers, at the DGI's discretion (Art. 741, Código Fiscal). Late payment: monthly surcharge of 5% of the unpaid tax or fraction thereof, capped at 25% (Art. 742); default interest at the legal rate accrues from the statutory due date. Willful non-filing with material understatement is subject to criminal prosecution under Art. 815-A (imprisonment of 2–5 years) and nullification of licenses before the National Customs Authority (ANA).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding tax on dividends paid out of Panamanian-source taxable profits (Art. 731-A, Código Fiscal). The 10% applies to distributions to both residents and non-residents; dividends sourced from foreign-source income of the Panama S.A. are exempt. No branch remittance tax applies to non-resident shareholders, but the dividend WHT is due at the moment the dividend is declared or effectively paid, whichever occurs first.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama has a very limited network of double taxation agreements (DTAs); only a few are in force (e.g., Korea and Singapore; Mexico and several other treaties are signed but not uniformly effective in all cases). To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident shareholder must: (1) obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from the home jurisdiction's competent authority, apostilled or legalized; (2) submit the TRC, a Form 744-annex (Informe de Beneficiario Efectivo) and an ownership chart to the DGI before the dividend payment or at the time of the reduced-WHT claim; (3) receive a DGI confirmation of the reduced rate where the payer is a large taxpayer; (4) if the 10% WHT has already been withheld, file a refund request with the DGI under Art. 299 of the Código Fiscal within the applicable limitation window. Practical effect: in the absence of an applicable DTA, the statutory 10% dividend WHT remains the definitive ceiling for the Customs Bonded Truck Fleet's cash repatriation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and technical assistance fees paid to non-residents for IP, software licences, telematics platforms, or trademarks: statutory 12.5% WHT (Art. 733, Código Fiscal). Leasing payments for trucks, trailers, or GPS equipment owed to a non-resident lessor without a Panama PE: treated as rent/royalty income, 12.5% WHT. Interest on cross-border shareholder loans or unaffiliated debt: statutory 12.5%, but fully exempt when paid to foreign banks or financial institutions without a Panamanian permanent establishment; treaty rates under the Korean and Singapore DTAs (where applicable) generally cap interest and royalties at 10% and 5–10% respectively.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 250,000 (aggregate annual related-party transactions in the fiscal year). If the Customs Bonded Truck Fleet entity enters into intercompany arrangements (e.g., transport fees with a foreign airline group member, management fees, intercompany loans, or warehouse subleases) exceeding USD 250,000, it must prepare and file the Local File (Form 750) and, where relevant, the Master File, in accordance with Executive Decree No. 56 of 2018, as amended by Executive Decree No. 44 of 2020. Penalties for failure: USD 1,000–10,000 per infraction plus TP recharacterization.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Any other method applied in accordance with the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines as adopted by the DGI
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama does not apply EU-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) comparable to BVI or Cayman; however, the territorial tax system and GAAR (Law 38 of 2017, effective FY 2019) require real commercial substance. A Panama S.A. operating the bonded truck fleet must maintain: (i) its principal decision-making office in Panama; (ii) payroll, social security (CSS) registrations, and at least locally employed dispatchers/drivers; (iii) physical custody of the GPS-sealed trucks and trailers registered before the Transit Authority (ATTT) and Customs (ANA); (iv) signed customs bond agreements and warehouse lease contracts; (v) minutes proving that management decisions are made in Panama. Failure to sustain substance triggers: (a) CAIR minimum tax as a punitive alternative charge; (b) denial of intercompany deductions under GAAR; (c) reclassification of the S.A. as a tax-resident conduit, exposing non-resident shareholders to Panamanian taxation; and (d) FATF/AML scrutiny under Law 23 of 2015 for trader-as-shell risk.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion (Defraudación Fiscal) and False Returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully understating Panamanian-source revenue from bonded road feeder services; fabricating GPS logs to shift income to a foreign-source exempt classification; inflating fuel or subcontracting deductions; paying non-resident suppliers for sham services without WHT; failing to file Form 744 for two consecutive fiscal years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil fine up to 200% of the evaded tax, monthly surcharges of 5% (cap 25%), legal interest, and clawback of the foreign-source exemption for the manipulated period. Criminal: imprisonment of 2 to 5 years under Art. 815-A of the Código Fiscal and Art. 254 of the Código Penal for aggravated fraud; fines of up to USD 250,000; administrative blacklisting before the DGI and ANA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign the return or knowingly direct the concealment are personally and severally liable for the unpaid ISR, WHT, surcharges, and interest via piercing of the corporate veil. The DGI may impose travel bans (alerta migratoria), freeze bank accounts, and order civil restitution. Foreign nominee directors face the same imprisonment exposure under Panamanian law and possible extradition under the Central American extradition conventions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT – Shell Company and Beneficial Ownership Violations (Law 23 of 2015, Law 52 of 2016, FATF)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Panama S.A. solely as an invoice-splitting or fund-conduit shell without genuine bonded truck operations; accepting cash cargo payments without SAR filings; failing to register ultimate beneficial ownership with the UBO Registry (DGI) within the mandatory timeline; executing ACH/Bank Wire flows to non-resident shareholders without documentary evidence of real freight services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering offences under Art. 254 of the Código Penal: imprisonment of 5 to 15 years and fines of up to USD 5 million; administrative sanctions under Law 23 of 2015 of USD 10,000–1,000,000 per breach; automatic forfeiture of the bonded warehouse licence and the GPS-sealed fleet; if the S.A. is adjudicated a shell, dissolution of the company may be ordered by the Public Registry.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and beneficial owners with knowledge or reckless disregard face personal criminal indictment. The Superintendency of Banks and the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF) may impose travel bans, asset freezing, and a permanent prohibition from serving as directors in the Panamanian financial system. Civil restitution is joint and several with the entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Withholding Tax Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Undisclosed related-party transactions exceeding USD 250,000 with a foreign logistics parent; absence of Form 750/Local File; abusive intercompany management fees stripping 80% of taxable profits; non-resident dividend distribution without applying the 10% WHT or invoking an unratified DTA; cross-border royalty payments of 12.5% unreported and unwithdrawn.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: TP adjustment with recomputed tax at 25%, plus 5% monthly surcharge up to 25% and legal interest; Form 750 penalties of USD 1,000–10,000 per infraction; the DGI may disregard the transaction and recharacterize it as a dividend, triggering additional 10% dividend WHT and 20% penalty on the misapplied credit. Continued failure can escalate to criminal tax fraud charges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing director, CFO, and any independent director who approved or facilitated the non-arm's-length payments are jointly and severally liable for the shortfall. If the foreign parent directed the arrangement, Panamanian directors remain the enforcement target; travel restrictions and disqualification from corporate boards apply under the DGI's compliance enforcement powers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Customs, Licensing, and Economic Substance Breach (ANA and ATTT)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the GPS-sealed bonded truck fleet without a valid customs bonded carrier licence or without the ANA-approved route authorization; breaking the customs seal or offloading cargo at an unauthorized warehouse; maintaining no local payroll, no physical depot, and no insurance in Panama while claiming territorial benefits; failing to pay the annual S.A. franchise fee (currently USD 300, subject to surcharge after 31 January).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Customs fines of up to 10 times the commercial value of the merchandise moved in breach (Ley 12 de 2018, Customs Law); cancellation of the bonded carrier licence; public registry dissolution if the S.A. fails the annual fee and permanent agent requirements; CAIR minimum tax recomputation at 1% of net assets for every year lacking substance. In aggravated smuggling cases, penalties reach 3 to 7 years' imprisonment and confiscation of vehicles.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for unauthorized release of bonded cargo; ANA can issue travel bans against the legal representative and order the seizure of the fleet; criminal liability for smuggling under Art. 258 of the Código Penal attaches to directors, customs brokers, and beneficial owners deemed to have control, with civil tort liability for the full customs debt.
